newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index slightly up on gains to Nafta.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index slightly up on gains to Nafta.

text.p: Slovakia's Bratislava Stock Exchnage (BSE) continued its recent listless trading on Wednesday, with the 16-share SAX index slightly boosted by gains to oil and gas storage firm Nafta.
The SAX closed at 169.69 points, 0.55 point higher from Tuesday, pushed by a 50-crown increase in Nafta, to 1,150.
However, the issue traded only eight shares.
Also other blue chips traded thin volumes, as only 341 shares were matched on the BSE's listed floor.
Steel maker VSZ fell 10 crowns to 640, on a volume of 81 shares, while oil refinery Slovnaft traded 12 shares, closing unchanged at 860.
Brokers said they still did not expect the bourse to revive soon, as there are no new impulses on the horizon which might draw the investors' interest back to the illiquid market.
Overall volume increased to 1,233,184 shares, from 1,014,702 shares traded on Monday, while turnover rose to 900.11 million crowns from 868.87 million.
Both volume and turnover were boosted by direct trades. -- Peter Javurek, Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521-8402
